I've been thinking about this for some time now, and I'd like to promote discussion since this place isn't a hugbox.

I like indie games. I play a bunch of them and find myself playing them more than AAA games these days. However, I find indie games that use indie games off-putting.

Why? I've played my fair share of pixel games, and most of them are shallow, ugly, or just not fun.

I think that many indie devs go for a pixel art style for one of 3 reasons:

  1. The developer never hired an artist and isn't a good artist, so they rely on pixel art / nostalgia / the nostalgia fad (Countless shitty pixel art games)

  2. The developer uses developer graphics and never hires a proper artist (Minecraft)

  3. The camera is zoomed far out, usually meaning that the game has loads of content, so pixel art is generally the cheapest / most efficient way to produce the art for the game (Terrarria, Starbound, Risk of Rain, etc)

  4. The developer actually appreciates pixel art as an art style (Shovel Knight, Freedom Planet, etc)

I feel like the vast majority of pixel art games fall into category #1.
A Discussion About Pixel Art Indie Games

I agree with you to an extent, however I think what you're interpreting as a problem with pixel games is actually a larger problem with the economics of indie game development. I've played plenty of non pixel art games that were utter crap and had bad artwork as well.

The truth is, the market is flooded with low effort titles. I believe it's that way for 2 main reasons: The average attention span for gamers is low, so it's not only difficult to market to them, but difficult to produce something they're going to want to play for hours on end. Secondly, with the market already as crowded as it is, there's no guarantee that your work is going to sell.

Case in point, I've been working on my indie game for about 18 months now. I'll spend at least another 2 years getting it to where I believe it's finished. But I'm a lone developer. I have had no luck recruiting a team to speed up the process. I'm doing everything on my own. The scripting, the writing, the art and music. Whenever I release info about the game, I usually get a couple hundred views. That's not good in terms of future sales. By the time it's complete, I'll have spent 3 years dedicated to this project and might sell a thousand or so copies. I'll make about 5-10 grand on it, if I'm lucky. By comparison, If I had spent those 3 years working a part time job at Wal-Mart, I'd make 5 times that.

There is literally no economic incentive for me to invest in a long term, large project. I'm not in it for the money, though. I already have a full time job, and I'm making my game because I want to make a great game, and for the love of the project. A lot of developers are in it for the money, though. It's their job and they have to make design decisions based on financial decision. Hence the market being flooded with low effort titles.

Here's my project by the way:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fJCY8x3oOhs

That was before I lost 2 months of work due to poor backup habits and a flood that took out my main PC. I've been slowly trying to get back to where I was and I'm almost there, but the loss was personally devastating and I'm seriously unmotivated at the moment. I'll get back on track eventually, but I'm working at a snail's pace right now.

I don't think that it's a problem with pixel games, but rather it's a trend in the industry lately. I've seen plenty of horrible 3D games as well, horrible 2D games that use a hand-drawn art style, and all manner of other low-effort titles. I think this might all stem from the "nostalgia craze" that started around 2005ish which inflated the prices of old video games and popularized old games simply because they were old.

Yeah, it's financial suicide to work on a game by yourself, and I wish that every indie dev could just make games out of passion, but there does need to be some kind of return for their work, whether it be praise or monetary gain.

I like the look of your game btw, but the name "Project Nostalgia" is a huge turnoff for some people. Still, if you got the right people to let's play it or some other form of marketing, it could be pretty schway for your wallet.

I know I am but a lowly peasant, but if I may suggest, perhaps think about putting a helmet on the MC and shrinking his head. His body's got a nice scale, but the head is quite large and scary. I'm also assuming that this is a Metroid-like game, so that might help fit with that type of game. Maybe have a punchier color for the outfit.

Still, you have a lot so far, so good job! Keep it up and you might have Nicalis ringing your door. Just consider hiring an artist and composer.

I know that I'm replying a bit late here, but the thing I failed to mention is that pixel art has a low floor and a high ceiling. Some games use pixel styled art out of appreciation for the art form while other games use it because it creates wider appeal / is cheaper to do when you're not shooting very high. A good example for this is GunWorld; it has pretty ugly, undetailed pixel art and the actual game isn't that good either. There's no reason that the "retro" style couldn't be anything else, but making low-res NES sprites with no shading or complexity is easy.

Don't take personal offense. Good luck to your team on whatever Civ / FE game you're working on.

While I understand why a gamedev without much artistic skill would choose pixel art, I disagree that it's the case for the majority of pixel games. While there are a lot of games that have shitty pixel assets slapped on, there are so many games that are enhanced by the genre. The style makes sense for games like Fez or Minecraft because of the block mechanics, and games like Shovel Knight and VVVVVV use them effectively as a callback to earlier styles. While there are plenty of people who use the style as a replacement for more detailed assets, pixel art can be really beautiful when done properly, and definitely has its place in the indie scene.
